topicName: Recording Tests with HTTP(S) Test Script Recorder and Proxies
content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Recording Tests with HTTP(S) Test Script Recorder and Proxies in JMeter"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Performance testing often begins with recording user scenarios rather than manually scripting every HTTP request. Apache JMeter provides a built-in tool called the HTTP(S) Test Script Recorder, which acts as a local proxy server to capture browser traffic and automatically generate test scripts."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Prerequisites and Setup"},{"order":4,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Apache JMeter installed on your machine."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"A modern web browser (such as Firefox or Chrome) configured to route traffic through a custom proxy."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Administrative access to install the JMeter Root CA certificate in your browser for HTTPS recording."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 1: Configure the JMeter Test Plan"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"To prepare JMeter for recording, you need to add a Thread Group and the Test Script Recorder to your Test Plan."},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Open JMeter and create a new Test Plan."},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Right-click the Test Plan, navigate to Add -> Threads (Users) -> Thread Group."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Right-click the Test Plan again, navigate to Add -> Non-Test Elements -> HTTP(S) Test Script Recorder."},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 2: Configure the Recorder Settings"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"Select the HTTP(S) Test Script Recorder element and configure the following parameters:"},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Port: Enter a port number, such as 8888 (ensure it is not in use by other applications)."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Target Controller: Select the Thread Group you created earlier to store the recorded requests."},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 3: Handle HTTPS Traffic and Certificates"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"Modern web applications rely heavily on HTTPS. When you start the recorder, JMeter generates a temporary root CA certificate named 'ApacheJMeterTemporaryRootCA.crt' in the JMeter 'bin' folder. This certificate must be trusted by your browser."},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Click the 'Start' button at the bottom of the HTTP(S) Test Script Recorder. This generates the certificate."},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Import the 'ApacheJMeterTemporaryRootCA.crt' file into your browser's certificate manager under 'Authorities' and trust it for identifying websites."},{"order":20,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 4: Configure Browser Proxy Settings"},{"order":21,"type":"paragraph","text":"Configure your browser to route all HTTP and HTTPS traffic through localhost on port 8888."},{"order":22,"type":"code","text":"Proxy Host: localhost\nProxy Port: 8888"},{"order":23,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 5: Record the Test Scenario"},{"order":24,"type":"paragraph","text":"With the recorder running and the browser proxy enabled, navigate to your target web application. Perform the actions you want to test (e.g., login, search, add to cart, checkout). JMeter will capture these interactions as HTTP Request samplers."},{"order":25,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 6: Clean Up and Refine the Script"},{"order":26,"type":"paragraph","text":"Once finished, click 'Stop' on the HTTP(S) Test Script Recorder and revert your browser proxy settings. Expand your Thread Group in JMeter to review the recorded samplers. You will likely need to remove irrelevant requests (like browser telemetry or static assets) and add HTTP Cookie Managers and Regular Expression Extractors for dynamic parameters like session tokens."}]
